questions.question: Which mechanism among the following helps in identifying a type during the execution of a program?
questions.explanation: Runtime type ID is the mechanism that lets identify a type during the execution of a program. Using Runtime type ID we can construct and use objects at runtime.

questions.question: Select the statement which are correct about RTTI(Runtime type identification)?

options.text: It allows the type of an object to be determined during program execution
It tells what type of object is being referred to by a base class reference determined by RTTI
Helps in prevention of an invalid cast exception in advance

questions.explanation: Runtime type identification (RTTI) allows the type of an object to be determined during program execution. RTTI is useful for many reasons. For example, we can discover precisely what type of object is being referred to by a base-class reference. Another use of RTTI is to test in advance whether a cast will succeed, preventing an invalid cast exception.

questions.question: Select the Keyword which supports the run time type identification?
What does the following C# code signify?

options.text: Determines the type of an object
Both Determines the type of an object & a simple deceleration

questions.explanation: The given expression determines the type of an object using the 'is' operator. Here, expr is an expression that describes an object whose type is being tested against type. If the type of expr is the same as, or compatible with, type, then the outcome of this operation is true. Otherwise, it is false.

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code snippet?

options.text:
a is an A
This won't display -- a not derived from B

a is an A
b is an A because it is derived from A

b is an A because it is derived from A
This won't display -- a not derived from B

"Both ""a is an A
This won't display - a not derived from B"" & ""a is an A
b is an A because it is derived from A"""

questions.explanation:
We have to include the line 'This won't display - a not derived from B' this is because 'a' is object of class 'A' which itself is derived from class 'B'. So, 'a' is a B

Output:

       a is an A
        This won't display -- a not derived from B

questions.question: Which operator among the following supports the operation of conversion at runtime without generating the exceptions?
Which operator among the following is used to perform the operation of boxing, unboxing, reference and identity conversions?
questions.explanation:
use the as operator, which has this general form:

     expr as type

Here, expr is the expression being converted to type. If the conversion succeeds, then a reference to type is returned. Otherwise, a null reference is returned. The as operator can be used to perform only reference, boxing, unboxing, or identity conversions.

The cast in b = (B) a is allowed

questions.explanation:
since a is not a B, the cast of a to B is invalid and is prevented by the if statement.

Output:

questions.question: Which operator among the following supplies the information about the characteristics of a typeof?
questions.explanation: C# supplies the typeof operator. It retrieves a System.Type object for a given type. Using this object, we can determine the type's characteristics.
